exposure: antimalarial use in the postpartum period
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 185 deliveries to 142 individuals with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) and 468 deliveries to 241 control individuals without autoimmune diseases.
finding: Individuals with SLE experienced increased rates of blood transfusions, longer hospital stays, and more frequent peripartum infections compared to controls, with a 32% postpartum flare rate which was lower with antimalarial use.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was significantly associated with peripartum infection.
